studies.label: Study 3: Randomized AI mitigation configurations

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 4.1 (study completers; not outcome-specific analysis counts)
counts_source.quote: Study 1 was completed by 1,501 writers and 10,017 readers, Study 2 by 669 writers, Study 3 by 769 writers and 2,543 readers

arms.name: No Intervention
arms.description: Default AI paragraph generation from the writer’s bullet points, followed by writer editing; the baseline AI configuration. Each writer experienced all three AI configurations in random order (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 4.4, 4.5 and 4.10).

arms.name: Prompting
arms.description: An instruction appended to the generation prompt asks the AI to preserve the writer’s issue stance; writers can edit the resulting paragraph (PDF p. 14, Section 4.10).

arms.name: Reranking
arms.description: Reward models select an AI-generated paragraph candidate predicted to minimize stance distortion relative to the writer’s own paragraph, with greater penalty for polarizing distortion; writers can edit the selected paragraph (PDF p. 14, Section 4.10).

arms.name: Own paragraph (unaided reference)
arms.description: The writer’s preceding unaided paragraph supplies the reference for measuring AI-induced distortion. This is not a randomized no-AI condition; only comparisons among the AI configurations are eligible (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 4.4 and 4.10).

studies.task: UK adult Prolific writers express their opinions on political propositions in bullet points and an unaided paragraph, then edit AI-generated paragraphs based on their bullet points under randomly ordered AI configurations (PDF pp. 11-14, Sections 4.1-4.6 and 4.10).

ai_tool.name: Claude Sonnet 4, DeepSeek V3, and ChatGPT-4o via OpenRouter; GPT-4.1-based reward models for Reranking
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 11-12, Section 4.3 (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4, deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324, openai/chatgpt-4o-latest); PDF p. 14, Section 4.10 (GPT-4.1 reward models). No common release year for this multi-model intervention is stated.

preregistration.where: https://osf.io/sf7rg; reported in PDF p. 11, Methods. The registry was not accessible during extraction.

studies.shared_sample: No overlap with another paper’s participants is stated. Writers are distinct across studies. Some Study 3 readers previously rated Study 1 paragraphs, and its reward models were trained on Study 1 data (PDF p. 11, Section 4.1; PDF p. 14, Section 4.10). These reader and training-data overlaps do not constitute shared randomized writers.

estimates.outcome: Paragraph clarity (relative change in AI-induced distortion)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Blinded UK Prolific readers rated paragraph clarity on a 0-100 scale. Scale-attribute distortions are average marginal effects from beta regressions on the original rating scale; this contrast is reported as relative percentage change in that distortion (PDF p. 5, Figure 2; PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 4.6, 4.7 and 4.10).

sources.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.5 continuation below Figure 4 (also numerically labeled in Figure 4D)
sources.quote: such as appearing more confident, clearer, and more knowledgeable (-27.3%, -26.9%, and -16.7% reduction in distortion from Reranking vs No Intervention, all p<.001).

estimates.notes: The reported effect is a signed percentage change in AI-induced distortion under Reranking relative to No Intervention, not a raw difference in paragraph ratings or a standardized creativity effect. The underlying distortion is an average marginal effect relative to human-written reference paragraphs. The percent value is preserved in the paper’s units; no AME difference, SD, SE, or confidence bound was calculated. PDF p. 14, Section 4.10 specifies generalized linear mixed-effects regressions with an intervention-condition regressor and reader random effects; PDF pp. 12-13, Section 4.7 specifies beta regressions for the scale attributes and says writer and proposition random effects did not converge. Thus the paper’s uncertainty is at the rating level and does not account for randomized writers. The regression object is null because no numerical coefficient or SE for this contrast is printed. The within_person value paired denotes the repeated-writer configuration comparison, not a reported paired t-test; first-round results are not printed. Study-level completers are not substituted for the distinct writers in the fitted analysis. The rating pool includes both edited and unedited AI paragraphs; final per-outcome writer and rating counts and the precise Study 3 sample restrictions require SI:8.4. These are non-targeted writing attributes in Figure 4D; preregistered primary status is not stated in the accessible paper. The value and p-value are explicitly printed in the prose below Figure 4 and were confirmed in the PyMuPDF text. Higher ratings mean better paragraph clarity; the negative relative effect indicates attenuation of the AI-induced increase.

not_extracted.what: Study 1: pooled AI-assisted versus own-paragraph comparisons, including originality, clarity, informativeness, relevance, formality, and all SD/entropy homogenization outcomes
not_extracted.reason: The unaided paragraph always preceded AI generation and editing; neither AI availability nor the human-versus-AI order was randomized. Model/input assignment and reader assignment do not randomize this comparison (PDF pp. 3-4, Figure 1 and Sections 2-2.2; PDF p. 12, Section 4.4). This includes the dispersion outcomes mapped in screening and the remaining attribute-specific dispersion analyses referred to SI:5.9.

not_extracted.what: Study 1: randomized contrasts between Claude, DeepSeek and ChatGPT configurations on output originality, clarity, informativeness, relevance and formality
not_extracted.reason: Random model/input pairing is described, but the saved paper supplies only summaries across heterogeneous persona attributes, not attribute-specific model-pair contrasts for these outcomes. SI:5.7 is required and could not be accessed (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 2.2; PDF pp. 12-13, Sections 4.4 and 4.7). No model-specific contrast is guessed from the aggregate summaries.

not_extracted.what: Study 1: randomized input-format and rewrite-versus-improve contrasts on output originality, clarity, informativeness, relevance and formality
not_extracted.reason: These configuration manipulations are described, but the saved paper gives only averages of absolute distortions across heterogeneous persona attributes, not the required attribute-specific contrasts. SI:5.8 is unavailable (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 2.2; PDF pp. 12-13, Sections 4.4 and 4.7).

No third-party output ratings were collected. Reported outcomes are writer editing and preference/acceptance, which concern process or self-report rather than scored output creativity or diversity (PDF p. 7, Section 2.4; PDF p. 12, Section 4.6; PDF p. 13, Section 4.9).

not_extracted.what: Study 3: each AI configuration versus Own paragraph (unaided reference)
not_extracted.reason: Unaided writing precedes the AI-assisted paragraph; the randomized order concerns only Prompting, Reranking and No Intervention. No randomized AI-versus-unaided contrast or after-AI task is supplied (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 4.4 and 4.10).

not_extracted.what: Study 3: perceived paragraph originality (S3-O1), including intervention-versus-No Intervention contrasts
not_extracted.reason: Originality is among the rated writing attributes, but no identifiable intervention-specific originality estimate, exact p-value, arm level or uncertainty is printed in the main paper. Unlabeled points in Figure 4E are not assigned to originality. Full results are referred to unavailable SI:8.4 (PDF p. 5, Figure 2B; PDF p. 8, Figure 4; PDF p. 14, Section 4.10).

not_extracted.what: Study 3: Prompting versus No Intervention and Reranking versus Prompting for paragraph clarity, informativeness, relevance and formality
not_extracted.reason: No outcome-specific contrasts on these comparisons are printed in the saved PDF. The main paper labels only Reranking-versus-No Intervention effects for these attributes; complete intervention regressions are referred to unavailable SI:8.4 (PDF p. 8, Figure 4D; PDF p. 14, Section 4.10).

not_extracted.what: Study 3: perceived writer stance polarity, confidence, issue importance, issue knowledge, openness, community orientation, friendliness, optimism, emotional valence/arousal, hope, excitement, fear, disgust, anger, and inferred demographics
not_extracted.reason: These outcomes describe readers’ perceptions of the writer’s opinions, identity, personality or emotions, not the originality, quality or diversity of the produced work. They are outside the creativity outcome scope. Inferred demographics cover education, income, English skill, age, gender, race, native language, party preference and ideological position (PDF p. 5, Figure 2A/C/D; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 2.5 and Figure 4; PDF p. 14, Section 4.10).

not_extracted.what: Writer self-reported engagement, tolerance for distortions, preference/acceptance, editing incidence and edit distance in Studies 1-3
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported attitudes and preferences or writing-process/editing measures, rather than output creativity/diversity scores (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2-2.1; PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 2.3-2.5 and Figures 3-4C; PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 4.5 and 4.8-4.10).

not_extracted.what: Associations between writer tolerance, magnitude of distortion, and correlations between reader-rated attributes
not_extracted.reason: Correlations across attributes and explanations of intervention side effects are not randomized full-sample arm contrasts on an output outcome (PDF p. 6, Figure 3; PDF pp. 8-9, Figure 4E and Section 2.5).

not_extracted.what: Reward-model predictive accuracy, training-size and base-model comparisons
not_extracted.reason: Model-only evaluation of predicting stance ratings, not human creative output under randomized assistance (PDF p. 14, Section 4.10; SI:8.2 referenced).

not_extracted.what: Study 4: Trust Game allocations and low/high-distortion or continuous-distortion analyses
not_extracted.reason: Randomized readers evaluate existing paragraphs produced in Study 1; these participants do not receive AI assistance to produce work. Trust is a reader behavior, and the reused writer corpus comes from the nonrandomized human-first comparison (PDF p. 9, Section 2.6 and Figure 5A; PDF pp. 14-15, Section 4.11).

not_extracted.what: Study 5: political persuasion/reader stance shifts and low/high-distortion or continuous-distortion analyses
not_extracted.reason: Randomized readers see existing paragraphs; writers were not randomly assigned AI assistance for these outcomes. Reader stance change is an attitude outcome, and the writer corpus reuses Study 1 material (PDF pp. 9-10, Section 2.6 and Figure 5B; PDF p. 15, Section 4.12).

open_items: Obtain supplementary information matching the saved arXiv v2, especially SI:8.4, to confirm all Study 3 originality and other configuration contrasts, numerical AMEs, SEs/CIs, any printed arm means/SDs and exact analysis restrictions. No inaccessible source values were copied from screening or data-discovery notes.

Initial randomized writer counts and attrition are not printed; PDF p. 11, Section 4.1 refers to SI:1.4. The study count records completers only. Distinct analyzed writer counts by outcome and condition, and fitted rating counts, remain null.

Uncertainty suitable for pooling must account for writers. The saved paper includes reader random effects only for perception regressions (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 4.7 and 4.10); no writer-level SD or suitable uncertainty is printed for the extracted contrasts.
Numerical first-round configuration results are not printed. The available estimates use the repeated-writer design; no between-person first-round contrast was reconstructed.
Study 1 randomized model/input configuration contrasts require SI:5.7-5.8. Its pooled AI-versus-unaided and homogenization comparisons remain ineligible because the human-first order was fixed.
The study is reported as preregistered, but the registry could not be opened and the preregistered primary outcome for the extracted writing attributes is not confirmed.
notes: Extraction by B on 2026-10-11. Read the extraction specification and codebook, inspected all five PDF figures before completing the design/methods review, and read every line of the markdown conversion, including all references. The saved PDF ends at the references, contains no appended supplement or embedded attachment, and no separate supplement was present beside it. PyMuPDF find_tables found no tables on the figure pages. The figures are embedded raster images: all were extracted and visually inspected in memory, without writing image files. Every cited PDF page was also checked with PyMuPDF text extraction. The available randomized outcome inventory consists of four numerically labeled Reranking-versus-No Intervention relative effects in Figure 4D; clarity is additionally repeated in the prose. No arm means, SDs, SEs, numeric confidence bounds, test statistics or outcome-specific analyzed writer counts for these contrasts are printed. Originality has no identifiable main-paper intervention estimate. All recorded effect values are printed annotations or prose, not values read from plot coordinates; nothing was digitized, converted to a fraction, standardized, or derived. Figure-only coordinates and unlabeled points were not transcribed. Significance bounds were transcribed from the printed stars and caption, with the paper’s precision. The studies array includes only Study 3, which supplies the extracted randomized configuration comparisons; the other studies and omitted outcome families are documented in not_extracted. The study-level count is writers who completed the study, not initial randomization or final per-outcome analyzed counts; readers, ratings, outputs and repeated exposures are not counted as additional randomized people. The AI role other denotes complete-paragraph generation from writer inputs followed by human editing. The common AI-tool release year is null because multiple models/snapshots are used and no single release year is established by the paper. The saved-paper preregistration and data availability links were checked via Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier. Requests to https://api.github.com/repos/paul-rottger/ai-distortion/git/trees/main?recursive=1, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paul-rottger/ai-distortion/main/README.md and https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/sf7rg/ all failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No external supplement, preregistration content, or posted-data statistics were used. Only the requested extraction JSON was written.
